text: Their relief did not arrive as celebration. It entered through small things: Balag's appetite, Enhedu's dry corrections, Ninsun no longer looking at every junction as though it concealed a verdict. Zik allowed himself to breathe without matching the walls. He shifted the journal beneath his arm and found it cool again.

text: Perhaps refusal could be recorded without being defeated. Perhaps a mark could be damaged and remain damaged. Perhaps the City, for all its reach, was not without limits.

text: The corridor lengthened beneath their feet. Turns appeared farther apart than Zik remembered, and the ceiling sank low enough to force Balag to duck. The City's breathing had stopped entirely. Without it, the silence felt sealed.

text: The darkness had not returned. The wall stood exposed in the torchlight, the three old carvings arranged beneath the fourth. Ninsun's X remained across it, but the cuts were no longer fresh. Their edges had rounded. Gray dust filled the grooves. A hairline fracture ran through the lower stroke and vanished beneath a patch of pale mineral crust. The X looked older than Ninsun, older than any of them, as though it had waited on the wall for the same centuries as the three completed marks.
